question.prompt: Annie and Bonnie are running laps around a \(400\)-meter oval track. They started together, but Annie has pulled ahead, because she runs \(25\%\) faster than Bonnie. How many laps will Annie have run when she first passes Bonnie?

solutions.explanation:
After starting together, Annie first passes Bonnie when she has gained one whole lap on her. Since \(25\%=\frac14\), in the time Bonnie runs one lap, Annie runs \(1+\frac14=1\frac14\) laps. Annie therefore gains \(\frac14\) lap during each such interval.

It takes four of these intervals to gain one full lap. Before then, her lead is less than a lap, so she has not yet passed Bonnie. At the pass, Bonnie has run \(4\) laps and Annie has run

\[4+1=\boxed{5\text{ laps}},\]

choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Find the time to gain one lap
